title: Fully-connected three-mode squeezed vacuum: Gaussian entanglement, steering, and collective photon subtraction
authors: Manjia Mai, Jifeng Sun, Teng Zhao, Ming Zhang, Liyun Hu
abstract: We investigate a fully-connected three-mode squeezed vacuum (FC-C3MSV) state, where all three modes are pairwise coupled through nonlinear interactions in a triangle ($K_3$) topology. Using the integration-within-ordered-product technique, we derive the normal product form of the squeezing operator and obtain the covariance matrix directly from the Bogoliubov transformation. Under symmetric coupling, the physical state is genuinely tripartite entangled for any nonzero squeezing, while the three Armstrong-type witnesses provide a finite-window sufficient experimental test; in the chain-type C3MSV only one of these witnesses is violated. We find that, despite two-mode entanglement, the fully-connected topology admits \emph{no} two-mode Gaussian steering ($\mathcal{G}^{i\to j}=0$) between any pair of physical modes; the steering resource is instead collective one-mode-versus-two steering $\mathcal{G}^{i\to jk}$, which is $θ$-independent and grows with $r$. We analyze independent vacuum losses and obtain critical transmittances for steering survival: under full symmetric loss at $r=0.5$, one-to-two collective steering disappears at $η\approx0.58$, whereas reverse two-to-one collective steering survives down to $η\approx0.502$ and the underlying two-mode entanglement persists for all $η>0$. Finally, we revisit photon subtraction using a normalized phase-space derivation. A photon subtraction on a single physical mode does not generate Wigner negativity on another single mode, consistent with the absence of two-mode steering. Wigner negativity can instead be generated when Bob subtracts from the collective mode $(b+c)/\sqrt{2}$, with a loss threshold $η_c\approx0.667$ at $r=0.5$. These results distinguish pairwise and collective nonclassical resources in the FC-C3MSV and clarify the operational role of the complete-graph topology.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates the fully-connected three-mode squeezed vacuum state to characterize its entanglement and steering properties. It establishes that while the state possesses genuine tripartite entanglement, any two-mode Gaussian steering vanishes due to the complete graph topology. The key finding is that nonclassical resources like Wigner negativity are only generated when considering collective measurements, distinguishing these global correlations from simple pairwise ones.
main_problem: The study investigates entanglement, Gaussian steering, and nonclassical resources generated by a fully-connected three-mode squeezed vacuum state (FC-C3MSV). It aims to distinguish between pairwise and collective quantum correlations in this specific topology.
main_result: The FC-C3MSV is genuinely tripartite entangled, but it exhibits zero two-mode Gaussian steering; instead, the resource is purely collective. Furthermore, Wigner negativity can only be generated by subtracting from a collective mode, not from single modes.
method: The analysis employs techniques including deriving the covariance matrix via Bogoliubov transformations and using specific entanglement witnesses (Armstrong-type) to quantify quantum resources like steering and nonclassicality.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a three-mode vacuum state coupled in a fully-connected (triangle, $K_3$) topology via nonlinear interactions. The analysis compares this to a chain-type coupling structure.
key_observables: Genuine tripartite entanglement, two-mode Gaussian steering ($G_{i	o j}$), collective one-mode-versus-two steering ($G_{i	o jk}$), and Wigner negativity.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter $r$, loss transmittance $\eta$, and coupling strength $\chi$. Critical thresholds for resource survival are calculated (e.g., $\eta \approx 0.58$ for one-to-two steering).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes symmetric coupling ($\chi_{12} = \chi_{13} = \chi_{23}$) and models vacuum losses using independent amplitude damping channels.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the properties of chain vs. fully-connected coupling. Other figures illustrate collective steering measures ($G_{i	o jk}$) and mean photon number versus squeezing strength $r$.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the state's properties using IWOP/Bogoliubov transformations, establishes genuine tripartite entanglement via witnesses, then quantifies the vanishing two-mode steering while highlighting the collective resource. Finally, it analyzes how independent vacuum losses and photon subtraction reveal the distinct nature of these pairwise versus collective resources.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical characterization of quantum correlations in structured multi-mode systems, specifically demonstrating a clean separation between local (pairwise) and global (collective) nonclassical resources, which is crucial for designing quantum communication protocols.
